The '''2019–20 Belgian First Division A''' (officially known as '''Jupiler Pro League''') was the 117th season of top-tier football in [[Belgium]].

On 2 April 2020, the Jupiler Pro League's board of directors agreed to propose to cancel the season early during the [[COVID-19 pandemic]]. Should this proposal be accepted, [[Club Brugge KV|Club Brugge]] will be awarded the title.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.goal.com/en/news/belgiums-pro-league-cancelled-and-club-brugge-declared-champions-/1te7euvc2td4k1rtsjj9zq410e|title=Belgium's Pro League cancelled and Club Brugge set to be declared champions due to coronavirus|last=Smith|first=Emma|publisher=Goal.com|date=2020-04-02|access-date=2020-04-04}}</ref> In the meantime UEFA has threatened to ban teams in Europe in case their respective leagues were terminated early without trying to have all remaining matches completed.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/uefa-threatens-belgian-league-european-135211851.html|title=UEFA threatens Belgian league with European expulsion|work=Sports.yahoo.com|access-date=9 April 2020|archive-date=11 September 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200911142142/https://sports.yahoo.com/uefa-threatens-belgian-league-european-135211851.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> The decision of whether to accept this proposal was initially meant to be decided by a vote at a meeting on 15 April 2020, but had been postponed three times.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.news18.com/news/football/belgian-pro-league-delays-vote-on-ending-season-for-the-third-time-2604553.html|title=Belgian Pro League Delays Vote on Ending Season for the Third Time|publisher=news18.com|date=4 May 2020}}</ref>

The proposal was finally accepted by the General Assembly on 15 May 2020, confirming [[Club Brugge KV|Club Brugge]] as 2019–20 First Division A champions.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sport.be/nl/jupilerproleague/nieuws/article.html?Article_ID=884822|title=Communicatie na de Algemene Vergadering|publisher=Jupiler Pro League|date=15 May 2020|access-date=15 May 2020|archive-date=13 June 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200613064954/https://www.sport.be/nl/jupilerproleague/nieuws/article.html?Article_ID=884822|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Team changes==
As [[2018–19 Belgian First Division B]] champions, [[K.V. Mechelen|Mechelen]] would have replaced relegated [[K.S.C. Lokeren Oost-Vlaanderen|Lokeren]]. However, as part of the [[2017–19 Belgian football fraud scandal]], Mechelen were found guilty of match-fixing at the end of the [[2017–18 Belgian First Division A|2017–18 season]], resulting in the club being relegated back to the First Division B and runners-up [[K Beerschot VA|Beerschot]] taking the spot of Mechelen instead. Mechelen appealed the decision with the Belgian Court of Arbitration for Sports, which confirmed that KV Mechelen was indeed guilty of match-fixing, but that according to the rules of the [[Royal Belgian Football Association]], relegation is no longer a possible penalty as the match-fixing occurred more than one season ago. KV Mechelen was thus allowed to play in the Belgian First Division A, but did get banned from participating in the UEFA Europa League and the Belgian Cup for one season.

==Format change==
While the regular season remains unchanged, the end of season play-offs have been altered somewhat, specifically the Europa League play-offs will now be played by 16 instead of 12 teams. Taking part will be the bottom ten teams together with the six top teams from the Belgian First Division B, to be divided in four groups of four teams. The four group winners will play semi-finals and a final to determine the team which will play the fourth (or fifth) placed team from the championship play-offs for the remaining ticket into the UEFA Europa League. This change allows both the team relegating from the 2019–20 Belgian First Division A and the [[2019–20 Belgian First Division B]] champion to take part in the Europa League play-offs, allowing these teams to bridge the gap of nearly six months without any matches as used to be the case in previous seasons.<ref name="po2">{{cite web |url=https://sporza.be/artikels/pro-league-heeft-beslist-play-off-i-blijft-ongewijzigd-play-off-ii-met-16-clubs~1559925221011/|title=Pro League heeft beslist: Play-off I blijft ongewijzigd, Play-off II met 16 clubs|trans-title=Pro League has decided: Play-off I remains unchanged, Play-off II with 16 clubs |work=sporza.be|date=7 June 2019 |access-date=7 June 2019}}</ref>

| match_STR_GNK_note = The match between Sint-Truiden and Genk was suspended with the score at 3–3 due to supporter violence. Initially, no points were awarded and the Belgian FA demanded to replay the match entirely behind closed doors and further penalize both clubs with an additional match behind closed doors, a two points penalty and a fine of 5000 Euro.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sport.be/nl/jupilerproleague/nieuws/article.html?Article_ID=871903|title=Bondsparket vordert match achter gesloten deuren tegen STVV en Genk|first=Gert-Jan|last=Weyters|date=10 October 2019|publisher=[[Jupiler Pro League]]|trans-title=FA request match without supporters for STVV and Genk|language=nl|access-date=10 October 2019|archive-date=13 September 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200913192831/https://www.sport.be/nl/jupilerproleague/nieuws/article.html?Article_ID=871903|url-status=dead}}</ref> On 4 December 2019, after both clubs had appealed the decision citing an incorrectly followed procedure in which the referee had stopped the match too soon, the final verdict was that the 3–3 result stood as final and both clubs were penalized 5000 Euro and were forced to play their next home match with part of their stand closed.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://sporza.be/artikels/gestaakte-stvv-genk-van-28-september-wordt-niet-herspeeld~1575479472631/|title=Gestaakte STVV-Genk van 28 september wordt niet herspeeld|first=Gert-Jan|last=Weyters|date=4 December 2019|publisher=sporza.be|trans-title=Suspended match STVV-Genk of 28 september will not be replayed|language=nl}}</ref>
